title: Nonderogatory → Cyclic Vector: The General Case (All Fields)
description: The nonderogatory → cyclic vector theorem holds for ALL fields, including finite fields F_q with q ≤ n where union avoidance fails. Demonstrates F_2 counterexample and module-theoretic approach.

meta.author: Classical linear algebra (invariant factor decomposition)
meta.assumptions: 0 axioms. 1 sorry: main theorem nonderogatory_has_cyclic_vector_any_field (needs structure theorem for f.g. modules over PID, not in Mathlib).

overview.text: The nonderogatory → cyclic vector theorem holds for ALL fields, including finite fields where union avoidance fails.
overview.proofStrategy: Module-theoretic: K^n as K[X]-module, invariant factor decomposition, nonderogatory forces single factor.

sections.title: F_2 Counterexample to Union Avoidance
sections.summary: Shows F_2^2 is covered by 3 proper subspaces, demonstrating that the union avoidance approach fails when |K| ≤ n.
sections.mathContext: Union avoidance failure over small finite fields.

sections.title: Annihilator Theory
sections.summary: Defines annihilator polynomial and states cyclic ↔ ann = minpoly equivalence.
sections.mathContext: Annihilator polynomials and cyclic vector characterization.

sections.title: GCD Annihilation (Proved)
sections.summary: Proves gcd_annihilates: if p(M)v = 0, then gcd(p, minpoly)(M)v = 0. Uses Bezout identity. Sorry-free.
sections.mathContext: Algebraic annihilation via GCD and Bezout identity.

sections.title: General Theorem (All Fields)
sections.summary: States nonderogatory_has_cyclic_vector_general: over ANY field, nonderogatory matrices have cyclic vectors. Requires PID structure theorem.
sections.mathContext: The main theorem for all fields.

conclusion.summary: This formalization demonstrates that the nonderogatory → cyclic vector theorem holds for all fields, not just infinite or large finite fields. While union avoidance fails over small fields (F_2 counterexample), the algebraic structure (invariant factor decomposition) forces the result. The GCD annihilation lemma is proved sorry-free. The main theorem requires the structure theorem for f.g. modules over PIDs, which is not yet in Mathlib.
openQuestions: When will the structure theorem for f.g. modules over PIDs be available in Mathlib?
Can the theorem be proved without the full structure theorem, using only rational canonical form?
